# Calibration report

*Generated by `python tools/calibration_report.py`. Do not edit by hand.*

The grade is rule-based: seven checks, 100 points, bands A from 85, B from 70, C from 50, D below 50 (`app/grading.py`). This report asks two questions and is honest about what each can and cannot show.

> The grade says how well a report is **supported**. It is not the ecological status of the stream: formal assessment stays with the OneAquaHealth field protocols.

## 1. What the rules do (a specification check)

Reports built to isolate one weakness, graded by the real grader. This shows the rules behave as designed. It is **not** evidence that the grade predicts anything.

| Scenario | What it isolates | Score | Grade |
|---|---|---:|:-:|
| First report: clear photo, good GPS, on the stream | the best a lone newcomer can do | 81 | B |
| ... and one other person reported the same nearby | corroboration, one neighbour | 89 | A |
| ... and two other people | corroboration, two neighbours | 95 | A |
| Proven observer (3 of 3 earlier reports confirmed), lone report | track record on its own | 86 | A |
| No photo, two neighbours agree | the photo is worth the most points (30) | 55 | C |
| Blurry, dark, small photo | photo quality | 51 | C |
| Poor GPS (150 m), 1 km from any stream | location checks | 61 | C |
| Photo taken 5 days before the report | photo time | 71 | B |
| A nearby all-clear within 48 h contradicts it | contradiction (a different person, 100 m away) | 78 | B |
| Observer mostly not confirmed (1 of 5 earlier reports) | track record, the bad end | 78 | B |
| Worst case: no photo, no GPS accuracy, off stream, 0 of 4 confirmed | everything wrong at once | 18 | D |

**What this tells us, including the weaknesses**

- A lone newcomer tops out at **B** (81/100): grade A needs a second person nearby or a proven track record. That is intended.
- A single agreeing neighbour lifts a lone report from B to A. This is generous: agreement is cheap to fake. The *trust level* (not the grade) is what resists it, because it counts different people spread in time or place, caps corroborations per account per day, and needs an expert for decision grade.
- A contradicting all-clear costs a report only 3 points (still B). The expert, not the grade, settles contradictions.
- An observer whose earlier reports were mostly not confirmed still gets B (78/100): track record is worth at most 10 points.
- A report with no photo cannot pass 60 points, so it can never be better than C.

These are the first things to revisit once real decisions exist.

## 2. Does the grade predict what experts decide?

This is the calibration that matters: of the reports an expert decided, how often were grade A, B, C, D confirmed? Below is the **synthetic demo data**, so it only shows that the method works.

| Grade | Decided | Confirmed | Not confirmed | Share confirmed |
|:-:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | 1 | 1 | 0 | n/a |
| B | 11 | 10 | 1 | n/a |
| C | 0 | 0 | 0 | n/a |
| D | 0 | 0 | 0 | n/a |

Only 12 decided reports so far (at least 30 are needed before any rate means anything). These counts show the method, not the grade's accuracy.

The Standards page in the web app shows the same table, computed live on whatever decisions exist (rates appear once 30 reports are decided).

## 3. Limits we know about

- Experts do not review a random sample: health-relevant reports come first, so the reviewed reports are not typical.
- A grade may influence which reports get looked at, and experts read the grade's reasons before they decide.
- 'Confirmed' means an expert agreed the sign is visible, not that the stream is unhealthy.
- Thresholds and weights are configurable defaults, to be calibrated with OneAquaHealth ecologists on real field data.
- No real field photos or expert-labelled field data were available for this submission, so nothing here is a measured accuracy.

## 4. How to calibrate for real

1. Run a pilot where OneAquaHealth ecologists decide a sample of reports of every grade, not only the health-relevant ones, so the sample is not biased towards one end.
2. Read the table above on those decisions; adjust the weights and bands in `app/grading.py` and the thresholds in `app/config.py`; repeat.
3. Publish the table with its sample size, as here.

*Window and thresholds in force: nearby reports within 500 m and 14 days; advisory threshold 2 expert-verified or 3 community-supported reports of the same sign. Illustrative defaults.*
